chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Sulayman ibn Amr has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah Al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Jiblah, from Ali ibn Shajarah, from Sulayman ibn Amr Al-Ahmar.

key_terms.الصَّفَّارِ: Al-Saffar, a nisba indicating profession or origin
key_terms.الْأَحْمَرِ: Al-Ahmar, meaning 'the Red', a common epithet
key_terms.الْبَرْقِيِّ: Al-Barqi, a nisba indicating origin from Barqa
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him

ai.seo_question: What is the chain of narrators for Sulayman ibn Amr in Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* provides a detailed *isnad* (chain of transmission) linking Shaykh al-Saduq to Sulayman ibn Amr Al-Ahmar, highlighting the scholarly rigor in verifying the reliability of narrators in Shia hadith literature. By explicitly tracing the lineage through prominent figures like Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, al-Saduq underscores the authenticity and continuity of the Imami scholarly tradition. This method of cross-referencing chains serves to authenticate the legal and theological content attributed to Sulayman, ensuring its acceptance within the broader corpus of Shia jurisprudence.
